headlines.title: Search continues for hit-and-run driver who struck teen bike rider in Hayward
headlines.description: A 15-year-old boy is asking for the public’s help in finding the driver who struck him while he was riding a bike in Hayward last month. Jefferson Pineda was seriously injured at about 7:20 p.m. on Sept. 14 while riding an e-bike at the intersection of Alice and B streets near the Hayward BART station. Police said the driver ran a stop sign, struck Pineda and didn’t stop. Pineda broke several bones and is still recovering from head and leg injuries. Pineda and his family have been asking residents if their cameras captured the collision or images of the hit-and-run suspect. “Face up, be a man or something,” Pineda said. “You hit a kid. How are you going to hit a kid and just leave him there? What if he dies or something? What if I would’ve died? I don’t want to ride ever again, to be honest.” Anyone with information about the case is asked to contact Hayward police.

headlines.title: Woman dies after shooting in downtown Oakland
headlines.description: A woman died following a shooting in Oakland on early Sunday morning, according to the coroner’s office. The shooting occurred in the area of Harrison and 14th streets around 1:35 a.m., the Oakland Fire Department said. According to a report from The Mercury News, police said the woman got into a confrontation before someone shot her. The Oakland Fire Department confirmed the woman was transported by ambulance to a hospital. The coroner’s office confirmed that one person died from the shooting, and the police department later stated it was the woman who had been wounded. The police department said a woman from Richmond was arrested in connection with the incident. It has not yet been disclosed what sparked the alleged confrontation. The victim is not from Oakland, but police have not released her hometown or why she was visiting the city, The Mercury News reports.

headlines.title: 3 people dead after shooting in Marin County
headlines.description: Three people died following a shooting in Marin County on Sunday, according to the sheriff’s office. The sheriff’s office said it received a 911 call just after 5 p.m. reporting shots fired at a home on Strawberry Circle. Authorities said the reporting party was inside the home and was able to exit it. At the scene, deputies established a perimeter and safely entered the home, where they found three people dead, authorities said. The sheriff’s office said it’s waiting to obtain a search warrant to enter the home, and the coroner’s office would be en route to the scene. Authorities did not release the connection between the victims.

headlines.title: Crash involving wrong-way driver prompts partial closure of Hwy. 4 in Concord area
headlines.description: A crash involving a wrong-way driver prompted the partial closure of Highway 4 in the Concord area, the California Highway Patrol said. CHP said around 6 p.m., a Honda Civic involved in a pursuit with the Contra Costa County Sheriff’s Office crashed into a vehicle and entered the eastbound lanes of the highway, driving in the wrong direction. The car clipped a couple of other vehicles before crashing head-on into a Jeep Grand Cherokee, CHP said. Authorities said the Honda flipped in the process and the woman driver suffered moderate injuries. According to CHP, the woman and her passenger ran away before being caught by deputies. CHP said the crash prompted the closure of lanes one through four eastbound Highway 4, west of Willow Pass. Authorities said time for reopening is still not available. Drivers are advised to use alternative routes. This story uses functionality that may not work in our app. Click here to open the story in your web browser.

headlines.title: Person dies after multi-vehicle crash on Hwy. 101 in San Jose
headlines.description: A person died following a multi-vehicle crash that prompted a partial closure of Highway 101 on Saturday morning in San Jose, the California Highway Patrol said. CHP said the crash occurred around 5:30 a.m., north of the Tully Road off-ramp. Authorities said initial reports indicated the incident involved one vehicle, but it was later determined multiple vehicles were involved. One person died in the crash, according to CHP. Authorities were also advised of a possible ejection and a trapped occupant, adding many vehicles sustained major damage. The crash prompted the closure of all southbound lanes on Highway 101. The lanes reopened around 9 a.m.

headlines.title: Big crowds enjoy Blue Angels air show as part of San Francisco Fleet Week
headlines.description: One of the highlights of the Fleet Week in San Francisco are the U.S. Navy Blue Angels. The Blue Angels soared and roared over San Francisco Saturday – and this time, they were visible. The air show kicked off just after noon, bringing out aviation fans to watch the different aircraft soaring overheard. This time, the conditions were better than Friday’s, when the cloudy skies cut the Blue Angels show short. “It’s amazing, we have been spellbound to watch and see how amazing it is what they do and how they do it, right?” Canada resident Lana said. “I have been looking at the weather and thinking what is the best day to go out, and today seemed like a good day,” San Francisco resident Allison said. Many hope the weather will cooperate again on Sunday. Marine Corps pilot Major Andrew Sanchez spoke with NBC Bay Area and shared some insight about his experience. “I fly the F-35B, which is a fifth-generation fighter aircraft flown primarily by the United States Marine Corps because I’m a Marine Corps pilot,” he said. “The thing that makes the F-35B unique, aside from being flown by the Marine Corps, is that and can really hover like a helicopter and it’s designed to land vertically on ships.” The Ship Tours had people lining up along the Embarcadero. One of those ships was the USS Ashland. Fleet Week festivities continue on Sunday. For more information, visit our Fleet Week guide.

headlines.title: Valkyries sweep Aces to clinch first-ever WNBA Finals berth, will face Dream
headlines.description: In just Year 2 of the franchise’s existence, the Golden State Valkyries are headed to the WNBA Finals. After winning Games 1 and 2 at home, the Valkyries defeated the Las Vegas Aces 87-77 in overtime on Friday at Michelob ULTRA Arena to complete a three-game sweep in the semifinals. Kayla Thornton led the way with 18 points and nine rebounds, while Kiah Stokes tallied 11 points, 10 rebounds and three blocks in a thrilling victory to clinch their spot in the WNBA Finals. Next, Golden State will take on the Atlanta Dream, who completed a three-game sweep of their own on Friday to take down the New York Liberty in the other semifinals matchup. The Valkyries won all three regular-season matchups against the Dream, with each game taking place within a two-week span between June 24 and July 4. Game 1 of the WNBA Finals, a best-of-seven series, will tip off on Saturday, Oct. 17 at 12:30 p.m. PT at “Ballhalla,” as the Valkyries have dubbed their home floor at Chase Center. Golden State owns home-court advantage for the series thanks to its higher seed; Games 1, 2, 5 and 7 — the latter two only if necessary — will be held at Chase Center. Despite trailing by nine points at halftime and as much as 11 early in the second half, the Valkyries went on a 17-0 run in the third quarter to claim their first lead of the night over the Aces. The Aces wouldn’t go down easy at home, though, re-taking a six-point advantage in the final three minutes. Three-time reigning WNBA MVP A’ja Wilson wasn’t at her best on Friday, but she still led all scorers with 21 points to go with 10 rebounds. But the Valkyries battled back again, responding with an 8-0 run that helped eventually force overtime. In the extra period, Golden State’s top-ranked defense — along with their leading scorer Gabby Williams — took control. Williams scored eight of her 16 points in overtime, and the Valkyries outscored the Aces 16-6 in the frame. In 2025, the Valkyries made the WNBA playoffs in their inaugural season, losing in the first round to the Minnesota Lynx. A year later, Golden State is four wins away from bringing home a title — and quickly satisfying owner Joe Lacob’s confident declaration that the team would win a championship within its first five seasons. headlines.title: Santa Rosa police looking for missing girl and 19-year-old
headlines.description: Santa Rosa police said they are looking for a 13-year-old and a 19-year-old man believed to be traveling together. Police said 13-year-old Deanna Mendoza Pfoutz was reported missing on Oct. 1 and 19-year-old Jaden Wilson was reported missing on Oct. 5 but was last seen the day after Pfoutz was reported missing. Authorities said Mendoza Pfoutz is approximately 4 feet 11 inches tall and weighs approximately 120 pounds. They said she has brown hair and hazel eyes and was last seen wearing a grey t-shirt, black pajama pants, black shoes, and carrying a black backpack. Wilson is approximately 5 feet 4 inches tall and weighs approximately 120 pounds, according to police. They said he has black hair, brown eyes and was last seen wearing a black sweatshirt and black pants. The two were reportedly last seen together in Petaluma on Oct 4, and again in Santa Rosa on Oct. 5, according to the police department. Authorities noted Wilson has a medical condition that requires treatment, and officers are concerned for his well-being. They ask anyone that finds them or has any information to contact their local law enforcement agency.

headlines.title: Bay Area voter guide: What to know about the November 2026 election
headlines.description: What to Know — Election Day is Nov. 3, 2026 California will choose a new governor to replace Gavin Newsom, who terms out after this year. The choices are Democrat Xavier Becerra and Republican Steve Hilton. Voters will decide 14 state propositions. Regional sales tax Measure RTM, the Connect Bay Area Transit Initiative, aims to increase funds for public transit. California’s Congressional District 11 race features Scott Wiener and Connie Chan competing to succeed Nancy Pelosi. Aisha Wahab and Melissa Hernandez will face off again after a special election in August where Wahab secured victory to serve the remainder of former California U.S. Rep. Eric Swalwell’s term. All 80 California Assembly seats are up for reelection, as well as 20 Senate seats. California’s general election is Nov. 3, with statewide races and propositions as well as key local races and measures across the Bay Area. Here’s what you need to know to cast your ballot, including important dates and deadlines, how to register or check your status, where and when to vote, and what’s on the ballot. In this guide: Key election dates Check voter registration status How to register to vote How to find your polling place What to bring to your polling place How to track your mail-in ballot Why is California choosing a new governor? 14 California propositions What to watch Alameda County What to watch Contra Costa County What to watch Napa County What to watch San Francisco What to watch San Mateo County What to watch Santa Clara County What to watch Solano County County election offices Key election dates The last day to register to vote for the Nov. 3 general election is Oct. 19. County election officials will start mailing ballots by Oct. 5. Ballot drop-off locations open on Oct. 6 Last day to register to vote for the general election is Oct. 19. First vote centers open for early in-person voting in all Voter’s Choice Act counties on Oct. 24. In person early voting locations in the state open on Oct. 31. Election Day, Nov. 3, is the last day to vote in-person or return a ballot by 8 p.m. Polls will be open from 7 a.m. to 8 p.m. Vote-by-mail ballots must be postmarked no later than Nov. 3. If mailing on election day, get a hand-stamped postmark from a postal employee inside a post office. Visit the California Secretary of State’s website for a full list of key dates and deadlines. Check voter registration status Voters can check their registration at voterstatus.sos.ca.gov to confirm their mailing address and voting status. How to register to vote California residents can register to vote in elections at registertovote.ca.gov. Note Oct. 19 is the last day to register for the general election. Same day voter registration window will be open from Oct. 20 up to the Nov. 3 election day. Visit caearlyvoting.sos.ca.gov for a list of early voting locations to complete same day registration. How to find your polling place Visit the California Secretary of State’s website, where you can input your address to find your polling location and see what is on your ballot. Voters can also visit their county elections office for more information. Scroll down to the Bay Area county election offices section of this guide for further contact information. What to bring to your polling place Voters usually are not required to show identification to a polling place worker before casting a ballot, according to the Secretary of State’s website. There are some instances when providing identification is required: Voting for the first time after registering to vote by mail and did not provide a driver license number California identification number or the last four digits of social security number are missing on registration form In these cases voters should plan to bring identification to a polling place or bring a copy of it with their vote-by-mail ballot. The Secretary of State says the following are acceptable forms of identification: Passport Driver license Official state identification card Student identification card Copy of recent utility bill Sample ballot booklet received from county elections office Any document received by a government agency How to track your mail-in ballot Voters can track their vote-by-mail ballot and confirm it has been received by using the state’s Where’s My Ballot? tool at california.ballottrax.net/voter/. Ballots mailed in may take a few days to appear on the website. Why is California choosing a new governor? Gov. Gavin Newsom terms out after this year and voters will choose between Democrat Xavier Becerra and Republican Steve Hilton, who both advanced to the general election after a wild primary. Becerra has served as former President Joe Biden’s top health official and oversaw the response to the coronavirus pandemic. He was also the California’s attorney general during President Donald Trump’s first term and has more than two decades of experience as a congressmember. Hilton was a conservative commentator with a show on Fox News for six years. He also worked as an adviser to former British prime minister David Cameron. What are the 14 California propositions voters will decide in the November election? Here’s a list of the California propositions on the November ballot. Use the expandable graphic below for a breakdown on what to know about each measure. 2026 California Ballot Propositions Click on a proposition to see more information about what will happen if it does or doesn’t pass. Source: NBC Staff Reports • Interactive: Annetta Stogniew Regional measure to watch Measure RTM: The Connect Bay Area Transit Initiative, is a regional sales tax aimed at increasing funds for public transit. It includes 5 Bay Area counties: Alameda, Contra Costa, San Francisco, San Mateo, and Santa Clara. Races and measures to watch in Alameda County California Congressional District 14: California lawmaker Aisha Wahab and Bay Area Rapid Transit Director Melissa Hernandez will face off again to determine who will serve the next full two-year term. Wahab topped Hernandez in an August special election to serve the remainder of former California U.S. Rep. Eric Swalwell’s term. Swalwell resigned from Congress earlier this year after sexual assault and misconduct allegations. District 14 includes the East Bay cities such as Fremont, Hayward and Livermore. Measure X in Berkeley: Would establish 10% limit on annual rent increases and other changes to the city’s rent ordinance. Measure Y in Berkeley: Parcel tax to pay for arts projects. Measure Z in Berkeley: Parcel tax to fund a public bank. Measure AA in Berkeley: Increase soda tax (not assigned) Measure EE in Oakland: Shift city to a strong mayor system. Measure FF in Oakland: Eliminate foreclosure exemption from property transfer tax. 🗳️ For a complete list of races and measures on the ballot in Alameda County and additional election information, visit the Alameda County Elections website. Races and measures to watch in Contra Costa County In Contra Costa County, several county board of education seats are open. In Richmond, residents will vote on a new mayor while voters in San Pablo will weigh in on Measure S, which would limit rent increases. 🗳️ For a complete list of races and measures on the ballot in Contra Costa County and additional election information, visit the Contra Costa County Elections website. Races and measures to watch in Napa County California Congressional District 4: Mike Thompson faces Eric Jones. Measure B in Napa County: Sales tax to fund wildfire prevention and open space preservation. 🗳️ For a complete list of races and measures on the ballot in Napa County and additional election information, visit the Napa County Elections website. Races and measures to watch in San Francisco San Francisco voters will weigh in on several open seats on the county board of supervisors and board of education. Proposition A: Give mayor more power to hire and fire department heads. Proposition B: Pave way for public bank. Proposition C: Increase the city’s annual contribution to an affordable housing trust fund. Proposition D: New barriers to placing measures on the ballot. Proposition E: Changes to city contracting. Proposition G: Reopen parts of the Great Highway to vehicle traffic on weekdays. Proposition H: Parcel tax to fund Muni. Proposition J: Eliminate foreclosure exemption from property transfer tax California Congressional District 11: Scott Wiener and Connie Chan compete to succeed Nancy Pelosi. 🗳️ For a complete list of races and measures on the ballot in San Francisco and additional election information, visit the San Francisco Department of Elections website. Races and measures to watch in San Mateo County Measure E in Redwood City: Limit rent increases. Measure Q in Half Moon Bay: Referendum to block proposed farmworker housing. Measure U in San Mateo County: Create independent commission to draw supervisor districts. For a complete list of San Mateo County measures and races on the ballot, visit smacre.gov/elections. 🗳️ For a complete list of races and measures on the ballot in San Mateo County and additional election information, visit the San Mateo County Elections website. Races and measures to watch in Santa Clara County In San Jose, incumbents Peter Ortiz and Bien Doan are up for re-election in Districts 5 and 7, respectively, and there’s an open seat in District 9. Races and measures to watch in Solano County Solano County Board of Supervisors, District 4: Mike Silva and John Carli face in a runoff in a district covering Vacaville and Dixon. Measure E in Solano County: New tax on data centers and battery storage facilities in the unincorporated county areas. 🗳️ For a complete list of races and measures on the ballot in Solano County and additional election information, visit the Solano County Registrar of Voters website. Races and measures to watch in Sonoma County California Congressional District 1: Mike McGuire will face James Gallagher in a seat redistricted by Proposition 50. California Congressional District 4: Mike Thompson faces Eric Jones. State Assembly District 12: Eric Lucan and Jackie Elward compete in a battle between business and labor. 🗳️ For a complete list of races and measures on the ballot in Sonoma County and additional election information, visit the Sonoma County Registrar of Voters website. headlines.title: Fatal crash shuts down SB U.S. 101 near Gilroy, CHP says
headlines.description: A fatal single-vehicle crash shut down southbound U.S. 101 near the Crocker Lane and Old Gilroy Street area, just south of Gilroy, early Sunday morning. According to California Highway Patrol logs, the crash occurred at 3:57 a.m. when a vehicle left the freeway, rolled over and became pinned against a chain-link fence. The impact scattered debris across the area and trapped the driver inside the wreckage. Gilroy police and fire crews responded to the scene, working to extricate the driver. A coroner was requested, and the CHP later initiated a tow response. Authorities have not released the identity of the victim or information regarding what caused the vehicle to leave the roadway. The crash remains under active investigation by the CHP.

headlines.title: Oakland Roots play their last Coliseum match, fans say goodbye to the venue
headlines.description: Saturday marked the close of another chapter at the Oakland-Alameda County Coliseum, as the Oakland Roots Sports Club played their final match there after two seasons of calling that venue home. Their match against San Antonio FC ended in a scoreless draw. Fans continued to cheer, sing, and bang on drums throughout the whole match and stayed long after to enjoy the fireworks show the team put on over the Coliseum. Loyal Oakland fans said it was hard to say goodbye to yet another team at the Coliseum. The game started off as games at the Coliseum have for decades: with fans showing up early to tailgate out of their cars from the parking lot. Fans fired up their grills and played music in the parking lot, many reminiscing on their days of doing the same thing before Oakland Raiders and Oakland Athletics games in the past. ‘Los Roots,’ the support group for the Oakland Roots, gathered once more in the parking lot with drums, megaphones, and giant banners waving. They marched around the parking lot, then into the stadium, and across the field before the game. “We’ve been following them since 2018, and unfortunately today, it feels pretty heartbreaking, them leaving the Coliseum,” said Roots fan Martin Delgado. In March of 2025, the Roots began playing at the Oakland Coliseum, hoping to breathe new life into the aging but beloved venue. For that home opener match in 2025, the Roots broke league attendance records with more than 26,000 people. After the Raiders left the Coliseum in 2019 and the Athletics left the Coliseum in 2024, many fans were excited at the prospect of having a new team to root for at the venue. But as attendance numbers dropped, the Roots faced financial struggles. In early July of 2026, the Roots announced that they would not be playing at the Coliseum for the 2027 season, citing “limitations around event control, matchday flexibility, the fan experience, and operating costs.” In a release in late July, the club confirmed it was behind in its payments to the Coliseum and that with how quickly the agreement was finalized, “there was little opportunity to negotiate more sustainable terms.” By August, the Roots reached a “pay or don’t play” agreement with the Coliseum’s board of directors, which allowed the team to finish out the 2026 season. It is unclear where the Roots will play their 2027 season, though the team has several options it is considering. Short-term options for the Club include an Alameda training facility the club acquired relatively recently, which could be transformed into a venue for games. In the longer term, the Roots have their sights set on Oakland’s Howard Terminal site. The team reached an exploratory, negotiating agreement with the Port of Oakland, and a realty group to develop Oakland’s Howard Terminal site. The departure of yet another team from the Coliseum stings for Oaklanders and fans. “We are grateful we got to see more games in the Coliseum after the Raiders left, after the A’s left,” noted Jorge Bejarano with the Los Roots support group. “But here we go again.” “I hope that if we find a new facility, a new space that we’ll continue to tailgate and support our teams,” said Estefany Angulo of Oakland, who has been attending games at the Coliseum her entire life. All the Roots fans who spoke with NBC Bay Area said they plan to continue supporting the Roots regardless of where they play their next season. “Ah the Roots, anything for them,” said Martin Delgado, putting his hand over his heart. “Anywhere they go, we’ll always follow,” he continued. The Roots said attendance was 9,718 for Saturday’s match. At the end of Saturday’s match, fans were treated to a performance by Oakland artist Goapele, who recently joined the ownership group of the Oakland Roots and Soul Sports Club. Fans were welcomed onto the field, where children ran on the grass, and families laid their blankets down to watch the fireworks display the team coordinated from behind the Coliseum. “Sadly, we’re here one last time,” said Estefany Angulo, who then added, “Hopefully it’s not he last time, but if it is, it’s gonna be a core memory for me.”

headlines.title: Man sentenced in Berkeley Animal Shelter arson case
headlines.description: The man who set fire to the Berkeley Animal Shelter in June is headed to state prison. Peter Taraba, 48, was sentenced to 16 months. The incident forced the shelter to close for two months. Surveillance video showed him using a rock to break the window of the shelter, and then sparking the fire using an “improvised incendiary device.” Investigators say police seized Taraba’s dog the day before the fire and then arrested him when he returned to the shelter the next day. No animal was hurt, and the shelter has been reopened.
